record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: For the multiserver job model with a finite but nonzero waiting room, rather than either immediate service or immediate dropping, what performance results can be proved when jobs that cannot start service immediately may queue up to a finite capacity?

evidence.quote: An interesting open problem is whether anything can be said for the multiserver job model where there is a finite (but nonzero) queue capacity.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on multiserver job queueing models (since approximately 2020) emphasize that performance analysis is tractable mainly in two extreme regimes: the infinite-buffer FCFS model (where only limited stability and asymptotic results exist) and the zero-buffer dropping model (which is analytically tractable). The intermediate case of a finite but nonzero waiting room appears not to have been resolved; current literature treats it as an active open direction with no general closed-form or structural performance results reported.

status_evidence.title: The multiserver job queueing model (Harchol-Balter)
status_evidence.snippet: Almost nothing is known about the performance of multiserver job queueing models; the dropping (zero-queue) variant is analytically tractable under very general settings.
status_evidence.claim: Performance of MJQM with finite nonzero buffer is identified as an open direction beyond the tractable dropping model.

status_evidence.title: The Multiserver-Job Stochastic Recurrence Equation for Cloud Computing Performance Evaluation
status_evidence.snippet: Applies stochastic recurrence techniques to characterize stability of the FCFS MJQM; results focus on stability conditions, not finite-capacity performance.
status_evidence.claim: Recent advances address stability of the infinite-buffer model, leaving finite-capacity performance largely unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: The saturated Multiserver Job Queuing Model with two classes of jobs
status_evidence.snippet: Exact and approximate results for saturated MJQM with two classes.
status_evidence.claim: Available exact results are confined to special saturated or dropping regimes, not general finite-capacity buffers.
